hints.title: Pigeonhole Bucket Partitioning
hints.text: Sorting in linear time requires non-comparison techniques. What happens when dividing the range between min and max into n minus one uniform buckets?

hints.title: Intra vs Inter Bucket Maximum
hints.text: The average gap is (max minus min) / (n minus one). By pigeonhole principle, the maximum gap cannot occur within any bucket, only between adjacent non-empty buckets.

hints.title: Bucket Extremum Tracking
hints.text: For each bucket, maintain only its minimum and maximum elements. Iterate across non-empty buckets, computing the difference between the current bucket min and previous bucket max.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumGap(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        if len(nums) < 2:
            return 0
        min_val, max_val = min(nums), max(nums)
        if min_val == max_val:
            return 0
        n = len(nums)
        bucket_size = max(1, (max_val - min_val) // (n - 1))
        bucket_count = (max_val - min_val) // bucket_size + 1
        buckets = [[float("inf"), float("-inf")] for _ in range(bucket_count)]
        for x in nums:
            idx = (x - min_val) // bucket_size
            buckets[idx][0] = min(buckets[idx][0], x)
            buckets[idx][1] = max(buckets[idx][1], x)
        max_gap = 0
        prev_max = min_val
        for b_min, b_max in buckets:
            if b_min == float("inf"):
                continue
            max_gap = max(max_gap, b_min - prev_max)
            prev_max = b_max
        return max_gap
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard comparison sorts take O(N log N) time, violating the linear O(N) time requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bucket partitioning tracks min and max per bucket in O(N) time and O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should know how to use the pigeonhole principle to prove why checking bucket boundaries suffices.
